About the Forescout platform and Splunk Integration

Splunk Enterprise data analytics help organizations leverage the data that their infrastructure and security tools provide to understand their security posture, pinpoint and investigate risks, and create alerts and reports. Security operations teams must also rapidly respond to any identified threats, violations and attacks in a prioritized manner. Any delay in response can result in significant security risks. The integrated combination of the Forescout platform’s continuous, agentless device visibility, network access control, dynamic segmentation and workflow orchestration capabilities with Splunk Enterprise’s data mining and Splunk Enterprise Security (ES)'s security information and event monitoring (SIEM) capabilities provides a solution that maximizes insight, dramatically reduces risk and increases operational efficiency.

Security blind spots are removed by having Splunk easily consume comprehensive information from Forescout such as:
• Real-time inventory of all network connected virtual and physical devices across IT, BYOD, Guest, IoT and Operational Technology (OT), including new devices with an IPv6 address. Device data can also be sent without dependency on IP address for reporting flexibility.
• Endpoint information, such as device type, classification, network connection, operating system, applications, users, peripherals and much much more
• More accurate user and location context by resolving overlapping IP addresses and layering tenant ID with IP address in meta data
• Device security posture and compliance gaps
• Authentication, access, tenant ID and network location information
• Threat indicators on devices detected by vulnerability scanning

Use Cases

Capitalizing on Forescout's rich contextual information and policy-driven actions together with Splunk helps you tackle the following use cases.

Rapid anomaly detection and accurate trend analysis

Forescout discovers, classifies and assesses all connected devices; compiles this information in the Splunk CIM format and shares it with Splunk. The additional device information from Forescout includes user information, device type, device configuration, network access patterns over time, network location and security posture. Splunk correlates rich contextual data from Forescout with other data sources and uses this information for long-term storage, swift anomaly detection and accurate trend analysis.

Enhanced incident correlation and prioritization

Splunk correlates rich device context from the Forescout platform with other data sources to better identify and prioritize incidents. When Splunk receives alerts from other data sources about a suspicious activity on a device, it shares the information with Forescout. Forescout provides high-value user, network and device context to Splunk. Splunk leverages this additional insight to determine if a suspicious event is actually malicious or violates policy and escalates or reduces the severity of the event based on the device and user context, such as highly privileged or less trusted users.

Automated closed-loop incident response

Forescout scans all connected devices for indicators of compromise (IOCs) and policy violations in real time when alerted by Splunk. Through Splunk’s Adaptive Operations Framework, Splunk operators can initiate Forescout actions—such as isolating or quarantining potentially compromised or noncompliant endpoints depending on the severity of the violation. Forescout can also dynamically trigger policy-based mitigation and response actions until the deviant device is remediated. Forescout then delivers the results back to Splunk to close the loop. Administrators can view the entire lifecycle and final outcome of the event in the Splunk dashboard.

Architecture Overview


Forescout integration with Splunk Enterprise, Splunk Cloud and Splunk Enterprise Security (ES) is enabled by the
Forescout eyeExtend for Splunk module paired with the Forescout App for Splunk along with the Forescout Adaptive Response and Forescout Technology Add-ons for Splunk.

The Forescout App for Splunk provides customizable, out-of-the-box queries and dashboards to visualize Forescout data in Splunk, displaying a wealth of information such as:
• Device compliance status
• User types (registered corporate users or guests)
• Device types connected to the network and connection details
• Patterns of network access over time
• Policy trends
• Forescout system health information
• Incident response action status

The Forescout Technology Add-on for Splunk is a required component to streamline data transfer between Forescout and Splunk Enterprise. This Add-on maps Forescout collected device properties to the Splunk Common Information Model (CIM) and extracts events based on Forescout data. The Forescout Technology Add-on also maintains Forescout credentials for communications between Forescout and Splunk Enterprise.

Support for Splunk Adaptive Operations Framework with The Forescout Adaptive Response Add-on


Splunk's Adaptive Operations Framework describes a complete action flow, which includes requesting an action be applied to an endpoint device and tracking the status of the action taken.
This integration supports the Splunk Adaptive Operations workflow as follows:
-The Forescout App for Splunk maintains a list of available actions from the Forescout platform. Splunk can instruct the Forescout platform to respond to potential threats by applying any of these actions to endpoints that match search/trend criteria.
-To complete the action flow, the Forescout platform reports the status of actions applied to endpoints.

These closed-loop incident response workflows allow you to streamline security operations and minimize business risk by automating the incident management lifecycle with a complete audit trail that also helps with policy refinements.

In order to view the full How to Guide Version 3.0.0, click the following link:

[https://docs.forescout.com/bundle/app-for-splunk-3-0-htg] (https://docs.forescout.com/bundle/app-for-splunk-3-0-htg)

Other Forescout-Splunk resources can be found at:

www.forescout.com/splunk

apps.documentation:
Fortinet FortiGate Add-on for Splunk

Next Generation and Datacenter Firewalls

Overview

Fortinet FortiGate Add-On for Splunk is the technical add-on (TA) developed by Fortinet, Inc. The add-on enables Splunk Enterprise to ingest or map security and traffic data collected from FortiGate physical and virtual appliances across domains. The key features include:

• Streamlining authentication and access from FortiGate such as administrator login, user login, VPN termination authentication into to Splunk Enterprise Security Access Center

• Mapping FortiGate virus report into Splunk Enterprise Security Endpoint Malware Center

• Ingesting traffic logs, IPS logs, system configuration logs and Web filtering data etc.

Fortinet FortiGate Add-On for Splunk provides common information model (CIM) knowledge, advanced “saved search”, indexers and macros to use with other Splunk Enterprise apps such as Splunk App for Enterprise Security.

Dependencies

If used with apps that are based on CIM, Splunk Common Information Model Add-on will need to be installed.

Please make sure FortiGate FOS version is 5.0 or later.

Configuration Steps

Install Fortinet FortiGate Add-on for Splunk on search head, indexer, forwarder or single instance Splunk server:

Note: There is a 3rd party add-on for Fortinet named Fortinet Fortigate with FortiOS 5 Add-On with folder name TA-fortinet, which has conflict with Fortinet FortiGate Add-on for Splunk, so you need to disable the 3rd party add-on before you proceed.

There are three ways to install the add-on:

  1. Install from Splunk web UI: Manage Apps->Browse more apps->Search keyword “Fortinet” and find the add-on with Fortinet logo->Click “Install free” button->Click restart splunk service.
  2. Install from file on Splunk web UI: Manage Apps->Install from file->Upload the .tgz file which is downloaded from https://splunkbase.splunk.com/apps ->check the upgrade box-> click restart splunk service.
  3. Install from file on Splunk server CLI interface: Extract the .tgz file->Place the Splunk_TA_fortinet_fortigate folder under $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps-> Restart Splunk service.

Add data input on Splunk server:

Note: From version 1.2, the Splunk TA(Add-on) for fortigate no longer match wildcard source or sourcetype to extract fortigate log data, a default sourcetype fortigate_log is specified in default/props.conf instead, please follow the instruction below to configure your input and props.conf for the App and TA(Add-on).

Through Splunk Web UI:
Settings->Data Input->UDP
Port: 514 (Example, can be modified according to your own plan)
leave other parameters as is.

Note: the UDP port, 514 in this example should be opened in firewall for logs to pass through. If you choose TCP input and on FortiGate use "reliable"(tcp) mode for syslog setting, you will need to add the following in local/props.conf because tcp tranported syslog will have xxx <yyy> header as line indicator.(8514 below is an example of TCP port, you can choose your own. There is no timestamp header like UDP so you can specify the timestamp field in the fortigate log, in our case the precision is in nanoseconds so the time format is %s%9N. If your FOS version has time stamp in different precision, refer to: https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Splunk/8.1.1/SearchReference/Commontimeformatvariables)

[source::tcp:8514]
SHOULD_LINEMERGE = false
LINE_BREAKER = (\d{2,3}\s+<\d{2,3}>)
TIME_PREFIX = eventtime=
TIME_FORMAT = %s%9N

If you are forwarding FortiGate logs from Fortianalyzer, please make sure you set the format to syslog instead of the default CEF format.

Fortinet FortiGate Add-On for Splunk will by default automatically extract FortiGate log data from inputs with sourcetype 'fortigate_log'.
If you want to configure it to extract a self-defined sourcetype, copy the props.conf
in $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/Splunk_TA_fortinet_fortigate/default/props.conf to
$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/Splunk_TA_fortinet_fortigate/local/props.conf and change the source stanza.

replace [fortigate_log] with [fortigate], for instance.

Restart Splunk service for the change to take effect.

Verify the Add-on in Enterprise Security App

Available dashboards in Enterprise Security App supported by Fortinet Fortigate Add-on for Splunk.

  1. Security Domain->Access->Access Center
  2. Security Domain->Endpoint->Malware Center
  3. Security Domain->Network->Traffic Center
  4. Security Domain->Network->Intrusion Center
  5. Security Domain->Network->Web Center
  6. Security Domain->Network->Network Changes
  7. Security Domain->Network->Port & Protocol Tracker
  8. Security Domain->Identity->Session Center

Please note in FOS 5.6 version, the type field includes "", so in order for the fortigate logs to be recognized, please upgrade this add-on to 1.5 version.

For more information on the App support, email splunk_app@fortinet.com.

apps.documentation:
Technology Add-on for Netflow relies on flow data and SNMP data processed by NetFlow Optimizer and enables you to analyse it using Splunk® Enterprise or Splunk Cloud.

It provides CIM compliant field names, eventtypes and tags for NetFlow Optimizer data.

The Add-on can also be used to generate sample events for testing purposes, it contains samples of netflow data and config files for the event generator.

Setup after installation - Splunk Enterprise:

  1. The TA-netflow is expecting that the sourcetype of events sent from Netflow Optimizer would be set to "flowintegrator". To set it up please create the $SPLUNK_ROOT/etc/apps/TA-netflow/local/inputs.conf file, and add the following lines to it: [udp://10514] sourcetype = flowintegrator
  2. By default NetFlow Optimizer events will be stored in main index. In case you want to use another index, please create the $SPLUNK_ROOT/etc/apps/TA-netflow/local/indexes.conf file, and add the following lines to it: [flowintegrator] homePath = $SPLUNK_DB/flowintegrator/nfi_traffic/db coldPath = $SPLUNK_DB/flowintegrator/nfi_traffic/colddb thawedPath = $SPLUNK_DB/flowintegrator/thaweddb You also need to make sure your $SPLUNK_ROOT/etc/apps/TA-netflow/local/inputs.conf file contains the following: [udp://10514] sourcetype = flowintegrator index = flowintegrator

Restart splunk for the configuration changes to take effect.

Setup after installation - Splunk Cloud:

  1. Set up the forwarding to your Cloud Instance, the recommended method can be found here: https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Forwarder/latest/Forwarder/HowtoforwarddatatoSplunkCloud
  2. The TA-netflow is expecting that the sourcetype of events sent from Netflow Optimizer would be set to "flowintegrator". To set it up, on the UF forwarding to the Splunk Cloud please create the $SPLUNK_UF_ROOT/etc/system/local/inputs.conf file if it does not exist, and add the following lines to it: [udp://10514] sourcetype = flowintegrator
  3. [Optional] By default NetFlow Optimizer events will be stored in main index. In case you want to use another index, please create the index based on these instructions: https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/SplunkCloud/latest/User/Manageindexes On the UF forwarding to the Splunk Cloud please create the $SPLUNK_UF_ROOT/etc/system/local/inputs.conf file if it does not exist, and add the following lines to it, assuming that the new index was named flowintegrator: [udp://10514] sourcetype = flowintegrator index = flowintegrator

Further documentation can be found at: NetFlow Analytics for Splunk User Manual

To contact NetFlow Logic support, please visit: NetFlow Logic Support page

apps.documentation:
What it collects

Every 60s sensors; every 120s SEL (scripted inputs, interval configurable):
- ipmitool sdr list full / sensor values: one JSON event per host per poll to index=main, sourcetype ipmi:status, with per-sensor reading, units, status (ok/nc/cr/nr) and thresholds, plus chassis power state, last power event, intrusion, and BMC firmware/ID fields.
- Numeric readings: one all-numeric event per host to index=metrics, sourcetype ipmi:metrics. Sensor names are slugified into metric names: ipmi.cpu_temp, ipmi.45fan1, ipmi.p1_12v, ipmi.input_power.
- ipmitool sel list: each record indexed exactly once (high-water mark kept in $SPLUNK_HOME/var/lib/splunk/TA-IPMI/) to index=main, sourcetype ipmi:sel (fields: sel_record_id, sel_sensor, sel_type, sel_assertion, sel_data, raw).

Dashboards

  • IPMI Overview: chassis/BMC status card, current sensor reading table (mstats), newest-first SEL log.
  • IPMI Metrics: trend charts for Temperatures (any temp), Fans (fan), Voltages (12V/3.3V/5V/48V/Vcore/VDD/BAT patterns), Power Draw (watts/power/PSU/input/output patterns), and a live distinct-metric counter.

Searching

index=main sourcetype="ipmi:status" | stats latest(sensors.cpu_temp.reading) as Temp by host
index=main sourcetype="ipmi:sel" | where match(sel_type,"(?i)critical|failure|lost")
index=metrics | mstats avg("ipmi.cpu_temp") span=5m

Dashboards note: panels contain complete searches; do not add a leading search keyword when editing panels. Family charts filter by common BMC sensor-name patterns (IPMI sensor names are manufacturer-defined); add your vendor's sensor name to the panel's search IN (...) list if it uses an unusual spelling.

Prerequisites (IMPORTANT)

  1. ipmitool installed on every Splunk instance running the inputs:
    Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt-get install -y ipmitool
    RHEL/CentOS/Rocky/Alma: sudo yum install -y ipmitool (or dnf)
    SLES: sudo zypper install ipmitool
  2. Bare-metal server (or VM with BMC passthrough) whose BMC is reachable by the OS: kernel modules ipmi_si + ipmi_devintf loaded so /dev/ipmi0 exists. Confirm with: ipmitool -I open mc info
    The app auto-detects missing /dev/ipmi0 and exits quietly on workstations/VMs/cloud hosts.
  3. Splunk 9.x (input needs only the built-in Python 3; inputs set python.version=python3).
  4. An index named metrics with datatype=metric (app does NOT ship indexes.conf; metrics go to your existing metric index).

Configuration

Ship-ready defaults in default/. Override locally: local/inputs.conf, stanza [script://./bin/ipmi_sensors_events.py] interval = 60 (set disabled = 1 on BMC-less hosts). SEL high-water resets if var/lib/splunk/TA-IPMI/sel_last_id is deleted.

License

Source-available. Free for personal/evaluation/non-commercial use. Commercial use requires a paid license: michael@bentleypc.com. https://github.com/bentleymi/TA-IPMI

apps.documentation:
What it does

Every 60 seconds (per input, configurable) TA-Nvidia runs:
- nvidia-smi -q -x — full XML query flattened into one JSON event per GPU (dot-path fields, e.g. temperature.gpu_temp, utilization.gpu_util, fb_memory_usage.used, gpu_power_readings.average_power_draw, clocks.graphics_clock, ecc.errors.*), indexed to index=main, sourcetype nvidia:smi
- nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps + key gauges — emitted as metric events to index=metrics using props/transforms metric-schema config. Metric names look like nvidia.temperature_gpu_temp, nvidia.utilization_gpu_util, nvidia.mem_used, nvidia.power_draw, nvidia.fan_speed, nvidia.clocks_graphics_clock.

Included dashboards

  • GPU Overview — Single-Panel per-GPU status: temp, utilization, VRAM used/free, power, clock, fan, driver and card identity.
  • GPU Metrics — trended mstats charts over the metrics index for capacity/thermal review.

Searching

index=main sourcetype="nvidia:smi" | stats max(temperature.gpu_temp) by gpu_name, gpu_index
index=metrics | mstats avg("nvidia.temperature_gpu_temp") span=1m
Tip on dashboards: panels already contain complete searches; do not prepend an extra "search" keyword when editing panels.

Configuration

Everything is pre-configured in default/. To change interval or enable/disable collection, edit or create an app/local override:
[script://./bin/nvidia_smi_events.py]
interval = 60
[script://./bin/nvidia_smi_metrics.py]
interval = 60
The metrics stream requires an index named metrics with datatype=metric (your existing metrics index user keeps it — the app never ships indexes.conf).

Requirements

Linux host (or Splunk host) with NVIDIA driver + nvidia-smi on PATH. Splunk Enterprise/Cloud 9.x. Splunk's built-in Python 3 is used (python.version=python3).

License

Source-available. Free for personal/evaluation/non-commercial use. Commercial use requires a paid license: michael@bentleypc.com. https://github.com/bentleymi/TA-Nvidia

apps.documentation:
This add-on supports auto-classification and field extraction for the following Symantec Mail Gateway log components. Each sourcetype is designed to categorize and normalize specific log types for optimal analysis and correlation in Splunk:
1. symantec:mg:bmserver - Email filtering logs (SPAM, Malware, Attachments, Quarantine)
2. symantec:mg:ecelerity - Email delivery logs(Failures, SMTP)
3. symantec:mg:snmpd - Network monitoring logs (SNMP events)
4. symantec:mg:rsyslog - Mail queue and forwarding logs (queues , system stats)
5. symantec:mg:crond - Scheduled tasks logs (Cron jobs)
6. symantec:mg:brightmail - Security logs (URL Analysis, Errors)
7. symantec:mg:auth - Authentication logs (User logins, sudo access)
8. symantec:mg:quarantine - Quarantine actions logs (Email released/deleted)
9. symantec:mg:audit - Security audits logs (System changes, Quarantine events)
10. symantec:mg:system - General system logs (Resource usage, processes)
11. symantec:mg:dns - DNS logs of symantec
12. symantec:mg:mail - Email viewed by user logs (User viewed messages)
13. symantec:mg:syslog – Uncategorized Logs(General Logs/Miscellaneous logs)

apps.documentation:
TA-Tanium provides sourcetype definitions, field extractions, eventtypes, and CIM tags for data sent from Tanium to Splunk.

WHAT IT COVERS

- Endpoint telemetry (Tanium Stream): process, network connection, file, registry, DNS, library load, and Windows security events

- Threat detection: Signals, OpenIOC, YARA, and STIX match data

- Asset and inventory: hardware, installed software, discovered interfaces, ARP cache

- Security posture: vulnerability reports, patch status, open ports, scheduled tasks, drivers, run keys

- Operations: deployment and patch mean-time metrics, endpoint configuration audit

CIM MODELS POPULATED

Endpoint, Network Traffic, Network Resolution (DNS), Authentication, Change, Malware, Vulnerabilities, Inventory, Alerts, and Intrusion Detection.

WHERE TO INSTALL

Install on search heads, indexers, and any heavy forwarder that receives Tanium data directly. The add-on has no visible UI.

The add-on includes a `tanium_index` macro that defines which index your searches and eventtypes target. Point it at the index receiving Tanium data.

Full documentation, including supported data sources and the Tanium Connect saved questions each sourcetype expects, is in the Tanium Resource Center: https://help.tanium.com/bundle/Integrating-Splunk-with-Tanium
